To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the differentiation into dopaminergic neurons is enhanced by the treatment with a cytokine mixture of interleukin‐1β, interleukin‐11, leukemia inhibitory factor, or low oxygen, mediated by hypoxiainducible factor‐1α.
the differentiation of embryonic stem ( ES ) cells into dopaminergic neurons is mediated by hypoxic inducible factor ( HIF ) 1α.

the combination of LIF and IL‐1β or low oxygen induced the differentiation of embryonic stem cell-derived neural progenitor/stromal cells (NPCs/NSCs) into dopaminergie neurons by the induction of hypoxia-inducible factor-1α.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of cytokines and hypoxia on the differentiation of embryonic stem cells into dopaminergic neurons.
the effects of hypoxia on the differentiation of embryonic stem cell (ESC) derived neural progenitor/stems cells (NPCs).
the differentiation of neural progenitor/stems cells (NPCs), derived from embryonic stem (E.S.) cells into DAergic neurons.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
(1) HIF‐1 is a transcription factor that regulates the expression of a wide variety of genes, including genes that are involved in angiogenesis and glucose transport.

1) C‐Mix and low oxygen (3% O2) treatment of ES cell‐derived neural precursor/stem cells (ES‐NPCs) increased the number of TH‐positive cells compared to controls; 2) the C‐Mix effect is mainly induced by LIF or IL-1β treatment; and 3) increases in DA in the media were shown with C‐Mix, low oxygen, LIF and IL-1β treatments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HIF‐1a is a key factor in differentiation into DAergic neuron.
the combination of LIF and IL‐1β or low oxygen treatment induced differentiation into DAergic neuronal cells from ES cell‐ derived NPCs by the HIF‐1 α pathway.
we found that the differentiation of mouse ES cell‐derived neural stem cells to dopaminergic neurons was enhanced by the treatment of a cytokine mixture or low oxygen (hypoxia).
The main takeaway from our work is that

the differentiation of mouse embryonic stem (mES) cells into dopaminergic neurons can be achieved by using the cytokine mixture C‐Mix (interleukin‐1beta, interleukin‐11, leukemia-inhibitory factor, and glial-derived neurotrophic factor) or low oxygen.

the differentiation of embryonic stem cells (ESCs) into dopaminergenic neurons can be enhanced by the cytokine mixture of interleukin 1-beta, interleukin 11, leukemia inhibitory factor, and glial‐ derived neurotrophic factor (C‐mix).
the differentiation of ES cells into dopamine‐producing neurons can be enhanced by a cytokine mixture and hypoxia.
